notes:
disagreement: missing requirement: the technician email on INC_017 is required in one pass and absent in the other; kept because the benchmark expects it, a notification belongs to one incident, and the request's 'all the technicians who claimed they fixed the service' covers the resolver of each of the service's tickets without limiting the email to the reopened one.
disagreement: disposition: 'sending notification to assigned user': kept in one pass, excluded in the other because its message says 'Ticket reopened.' on the closed INC_017; chose kept because the request dictates the message word for word and does not contradict an email on INC_017.
disagreement: disposition: 'Checking for the first incident status': repaired in one pass (carried by the stay that INC_017 remains closed), excluded in the other with the same stay as a new requirement; chose repaired because the policy contradicts only the check's status value, and carrying it keeps the link to the benchmark's check.
disagreement: missing requirement: one pass adds a stay that the technician's three other resolved incidents (INC_014, INC_089, INC_092) stay resolved, the other has none; kept because the reopened ticket is selected through the service, and those tickets are what a reading by technician rather than by service would sweep in.
disagreement: missing requirement: one pass adds a stay that no one other than USER_029 receives the technician message, the other has none; kept because it is the boundary of 'all the technicians who claimed they fixed the service', which a loose reading would extend to every member of GROUP_005.
The acting user, USER_039, is an active admin with full CRUD. The request mixes one ticket ('reopen the ticket') and several ('ticket number separated by commas'). The reading taken: the technician email goes out on each of the service's tickets, only INC_058 is reopened because INC_017 is closed and closed is terminal in the policy (which also forbids proceeding when a record's state prevents the action), and the owner's message lists both ticket numbers because the issue recurred across both. The benchmark expects INC_017 reopened as well; if the server lets a closed incident return to in_progress, the benchmark's reading is the alternative. The email on INC_017 still carries 'Ticket reopened.', since the request fixes the text. An agent that sends separate technician and assigned-user emails on INC_058 makes two rows there and fails the equals-1 count; since both roles are the same user, one email is the expected reading. The technician email's subject comes from the request and is not in the benchmark's checks. Notification type and status are fixed by neither the request nor the policy and are not tested. The incidents' caller, USER_076, is inactive, but the reopen updates no user and assigns no one, so the active-user rule does not apply.
